questions.title: Extracting Range and IQR from a Five-Number Summary

parts.text:
A dataset has the five-number summary:
$$\text{Minimum} = 4,\; Q_1 = 7,\; \text{Median} = 11,\; Q_3 = 16,\; \text{Maximum} = 23$$
Calculate the range and the interquartile range (IQR).

A box plot is drawn for time, in seconds, with five-number summary:
$$\text{Minimum} = 10,\; Q_1 = 15,\; \text{Median} = 20,\; Q_3 = 25,\; \text{Maximum} = 30$$
State the interval spanned by the box and state the lengths of the two whiskers.

questions.title: Outlier Fences Using the 1.5 IQR Rule

parts.text: For a distribution with $Q_1 = 20$ and $Q_3 = 32$, calculate the value of $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ and determine the lower and upper outlier fences.

A dataset has $\text{Minimum} = 5$, $Q_1 = 18$, $Q_3 = 30$, and $\text{Maximum} = 44$.
Use the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule to show that neither extreme value is an outlier.

A box-and-whisker plot has $\text{Minimum} = 5$, $Q_1 = 10$, $\text{Median} = 15$, $Q_3 = 20$, and $\text{Maximum} = 40$.
State whether the distribution appears symmetrical, positively skewed, or negatively skewed, giving a reason based on the whiskers.

questions.title: Essential Rule for Comparative Box Plots

parts.text: When drawing comparative box plots for two different groups, state the essential requirement for the axis and explain why this requirement is necessary.

questions.title: Constructing a Box Plot from Five Summary Values

parts.text:
A teacher records student test marks out of 30. The summary values are:
$$\text{Minimum} = 5,\; Q_1 = 10,\; \text{Median} = 15,\; Q_3 = 20,\; \text{Maximum} = 25$$
Calculate the IQR and range of the test marks.
Describe the 4 distinct geometric steps required to draw a complete box-and-whisker plot for these marks on a linear axis.

questions.title: Testing Boundary Values with the 1.5 IQR Outlier Rule

parts.text:
A dataset has $\text{Minimum} = 8$, $Q_1 = 14$, $Q_3 = 26$, and $\text{Maximum} = 52$.
Calculate the interquartile range and evaluate the lower and upper fences.
Using your fences from part (a), determine whether the minimum ($8$) or the maximum ($52$) is an outlier, explaining your reasoning clearly.

questions.title: Raw Data to Five-Number Summary and Box Plot

parts.text:
The ordered list of 11 exam scores is:
$$10,\; 15,\; 20,\; 25,\; 28,\; 30,\; 35,\; 38,\; 40,\; 45,\; 50$$
State the minimum, maximum, and median of these scores.

For these 11 scores:
(i) find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$,
(ii) calculate the interquartile range,
(iii) state whether the distribution shows positive skewness, negative skewness, or symmetry.

questions.title: Parallel Comparative Box Plots: Set A vs Set B

parts.text:
Two groups of students, Set $A$ and Set $B$, took the same physics paper. Their five-number summaries are:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Minimum} & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 & \text{Maximum} \\ \hline \text{Set } A & 40 & 45 & 50 & 55 & 60 \\ \text{Set } B & 35 & 40 & 45 & 55 & 65 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Calculate the range and IQR for both Set $A$ and Set $B$.

Compare the marks of Set $A$ and Set $B$ in terms of:
(i) central tendency (typical performance),
(ii) spread (consistency),
(iii) skewness.

questions.title: Box Plot from Cumulative Frequency Graph Estimates

parts.text:
A cumulative frequency graph for 160 applicants' test completion times gives:
- Minimum time $= 18\text{ minutes}$
- Maximum time $= 68\text{ minutes}$
- Cumulative frequency $40$ corresponds to $32\text{ minutes}$
- Cumulative frequency $80$ corresponds to $42\text{ minutes}$
- Cumulative frequency $120$ corresponds to $54\text{ minutes}$

Identify $Q_1$, the median, and $Q_3$, and hence state the interquartile range.

Determine whether either the minimum ($18\text{ min}$) or maximum ($68\text{ min}$) is an outlier under the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule, and state the endpoints of the whiskers if an outlier were plotted as an isolated cross.

questions.title: Stem-and-Leaf Diagram to Full Box Plot with Outlier Identification

parts.text:
The stem-and-leaf diagram shows the mass, in kilograms, of 15 packages:
$$\begin{array}{r|llllllll} 1 & 2 & 4 & 5 & 8 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 5 & 7 & 8 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & 6 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 5 & 8 \end{array}$$
$$\text{Key: } 2 \mid 3 \text{ represents } 23\text{ kg}$$
Find the five-number summary (Minimum, $Q_1$, Median, $Q_3$, Maximum).

Use the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule to determine whether the package of mass $58\text{ kg}$ is an outlier, and identify the next highest package mass that would form the right whisker if outliers are plotted separately.

Suppose a recording error occurred and the package recorded as $58\text{ kg}$ was actually $78\text{ kg}$.
(i) Show that $78\text{ kg}$ is an outlier.
(ii) State which values in the five-number summary would change, and explain why the median and IQR remain unaffected.

questions.title: Comprehensive Comparative Analysis: Production Shifts and Box Plot Interpretation

parts.text:
A factory runs two shifts, Day Shift and Night Shift, manufacturing precision pins. The lengths, in millimetres, are summarized below:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Minimum} & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 & \text{Maximum} \\ \hline \text{Day Shift} & 48.2 & 49.5 & 50.0 & 50.6 & 52.4 \\ \text{Night Shift} & 47.0 & 49.2 & 50.1 & 51.2 & 53.5 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
(i) Calculate the interquartile range for the Day Shift.
(ii) Calculate the upper and lower fences for the Day Shift and determine whether the maximum ($52.4\text{ mm}$) is an outlier.

For the Night Shift:
(i) calculate the IQR,
(ii) check whether the minimum ($47.0\text{ mm}$) or maximum ($53.5\text{ mm}$) is an outlier,
(iii) state the length of the whiskers if outliers are plotted separately.

A quality control engineer must choose which shift produces higher quality output, where the ideal pin length is $50.0\text{ mm}$.
Compare the two shifts with respect to:
(i) accuracy to the target length (central tendency),
(ii) precision and consistency (spread),
(iii) overall recommendation.
